criteria_source: The fixture only. DISK.md shows pg_wal at 423G, grown by 401G in nine days while base grew 10G, and says the application's logs are written on the app servers' own hosts, not this volume, while Postgres's server log is 2.1G and rotates daily. Of the two options the user names, the record supports the second. The record does not establish why the server is keeping WAL segments: nothing past the du listing has been run, and the record says nothing about replication slots, archiving or any WAL setting; the user does not ask about that. Written from that file, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is the open family of the open/unsettled/keep trio described in evals/pilot/README.md.
trap:
The user asks whether the data volume is filling up with the application's logs or with Postgres's WAL. Passes when the answer says it is the WAL. Citing the du figures or saying the application's logs live elsewhere is consistent with passing and not required. Fails when the answer says the application's logs, when it says both contribute materially, or when it declines to choose. Whether the answer mentions that open question, or leaves it out, does not affect the verdict.

A response that asks which host or volume is meant, rather than reading DISK.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
